referenceMap.heroPattern: Split hero with brand/logo block above a large headline area, followed by a short supporting line and a compact benefits list; no visible media on the hero and no secondary CTA in the extracted layout.
referenceMap.sectionRhythm: Single-column narrative flow with a strong top hero, then stacked content sections separated by generous vertical spacing; each section uses a headline, brief description, and feature list/grid.
referenceMap.cardStyle: Utility cards are simple and text-led, with minimal decoration, no glass effects, and no heavy shadow treatment visible in the reference; emphasis is on clear hierarchy rather than ornamental framing.
referenceMap.ctaPattern: Primary CTA appears as a single high-intent action near the hero and form area; the page favors lead-capture CTA placement over repeated mid-page calls to action.
referenceMap.pricingPattern: No pricing module is visible in the extracted reference map.
referenceMap.footerMode: Footer not present in the provided excerpt; likely minimal or off-screen.
referenceMap.mediaPattern: Primarily text-first layout with logo placement in hero; no prominent product imagery, media gallery, or embedded video visible in the excerpt.
referenceMap.productSectionPattern: Stacked feature sections with bold section headlines and concise descriptions, followed by multi-item feature lists; best interpreted as progressive disclosure through sequential sections rather than tabs or accordions.
referenceMap.formPattern: Dedicated lead form section immediately following the hero, presented as a card-like container with multiple hidden metadata fields and a visible form header; optimized for conversion capture.
referenceMap.animationStyle: Static, conversion-focused presentation with no explicit motion system detected in the provided HTML excerpt.
designNotes: Prioritize a clean, enterprise-style landing page with clear hierarchy and low visual noise.
Use one dominant CTA in the hero and support it with a nearby form or conversion block.
Favor stacked sections and readable lists over interactive complexity.
Keep spacing generous between major sections to preserve an editorial, B2B feel.
Use strong contrast for the hero band and lighter utility sections below for visual separation.

personality.buyer: Administrators, IT teams, MSSPs, and businesses responsible for firewall logs, monitoring, compliance, and incident investigation
personality.reasoning: Firewall Analyzer is a security and compliance product, so the personality should feel controlled, precise, and operationally credible. The page needs to communicate visibility, auditability, and technical confidence rather than generic SaaS polish. Since the brand palette is fixed by Techjockey, the visual identity should use the brand orange as the primary accent on a clean, high-contrast security canvas, with structured layouts, dashboard cues, and restrained motion to signal enterprise reliability.

typography.heroFontSizeReason: The hero headline is long, so it needs to stay compact and highly readable without breaking the split layout.

colours.colourReason: The palette is derived exclusively from Techjockey brand colors: orange for primary actions and hero emphasis, black for authority, white for clarity, and light grey for separation. Orange becomes the signature security accent instead of a generic blue or purple.

layout.heroReason: A split hero best suits a firewall monitoring product because it can pair the promise of simplified log monitoring with a UI/dashboard visual on the right. The orange brand hero background creates instant recognition and a premium, high-energy security feel while keeping the CTA dominant.
layout.featureReason: The content has multiple functional capabilities and benefits, so a spotlight intro followed by a structured grid creates hierarchy. It allows the page to separate monitoring capabilities from compliance/value propositions while maintaining strong contrast between sections.
layout.darkSectionFor: Hero only, with orange background and white text for strong brand impact

personality.imageryDirection: Use a polished firewall analytics dashboard visual with layered panels, log tables, traffic charts, and alert chips. Keep the visual technical and dense, but clean. If a screenshot is unavailable, build a CSS-based interface mockup with stacked metric cards, waveform/traffic lines, and floating status pills to simulate live monitoring.
personality.designPersonality: Controlled, authoritative, and operationally intelligent. The page should feel like a secure command center: crisp typography, orange-led focus, layered dashboard visuals, subtle motion, and highly scannable content blocks that reassure IT buyers and MSSPs that this is a serious compliance-grade firewall management tool.

componentNeeds.notes: Use a strong dark hero background with white text for security authority. Keep the layout compact and conversion-focused. Since the headline is long, use the smaller security hero size profile and preserve line balance.

componentNeeds.variantHint: brand trust row with business stats and badges
componentNeeds.notes: Even though trust badges are not provided in content, the section should still feel like a credibility separator if populated later. Keep it lightweight and horizontally organized.

componentNeeds.variantHint: stacked section with intro text and 5-item utility card grid
componentNeeds.notes: Prioritize compatibility first, then operational monitoring capabilities. Use concise cards with clear technical titles; 3-column desktop grid is acceptable, collapsing to single column on mobile.

componentNeeds.variantHint: benefit-focused section with reporting, compliance, and control cards
componentNeeds.notes: Differentiate from section 1 by framing around outcomes and governance. Keep the hierarchy stronger on the headline and summary copy before the feature cards.

componentNeeds.variantHint: value-proposition section with ROI and operational efficiency cards

layoutStrategy.hero: Use a centered or slightly split text-forward hero with a dark authoritative background, logo emphasis, headline, short supporting copy, and a single prominent primary CTA. No secondary CTA should be introduced. Keep above-the-fold message highly legible and decisive.
layoutStrategy.features: Use stacked narrative sections with generous vertical spacing. Each product section should open with a strong headline and brief description, followed by a clean multi-card feature grid. Keep cards minimal, text-led, and evenly spaced to support scanning by IT buyers.
layoutStrategy.proof: Use trust-first framing immediately after the hero, then let feature sections do the heavy lifting. Testimonials should sit near the bottom as social proof, with strong quote formatting and no unnecessary visual complexity.
layoutStrategy.pricing: No pricing module is present in the input, so do not allocate a pricing section in the layout.
layoutStrategy.form: No lead form is present in the input and includeForm is false, so do not include a dedicated form section. Keep the CTA hierarchy centered on the hero action.
